conventions.convention: P acts on column probability vectors; P_ij is the probability from source j to destination i. The corresponding row transition matrix is K=Pᵀ.
The zero-sum space is H={z:Σz_i=0}; δ(P) is its induced ℓ1 coefficient, with δ(P)=0 explicitly stipulated when n=1.
Graph edges are j→i when P_ij>0. Executing the decomposition requires an exact representation whose zero comparisons terminate; the graph itself is defined for arbitrary finite real matrices.
The certificate algorithm uses exact rational P and y and an integer m≥1. It rejects invalid P, returns candidate-unavailable when Σmax(y_i,0)=0, and supplies an accuracy bound only when q<1.

Hitting statistics use the row block T=K_U,U for nonempty U satisfying the finite escape hypothesis. Exit length counts transitions including the final transition out of U; residual bounds use the maximum-row-sum matrix norm.
Uniformization requires ν>0 and ν≥max_j r_j, with P=I+Q/ν and source-column generator rates.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite nonnegative row-substochastic T with a positive path from every state to a row with positive escape probability, there are L≤n and ε>0 such that T^L1≤(1−ε)1; writing k=aL+r with 0≤r<L gives ‖T^k‖∞≤(1−ε)^a, so T^k→0 and ρ(T)<1.
δ(P)=½max_j,k‖p_j−p_k‖1=1−min_j,kΣ_i min(P_ij,P_ik), and ‖Pz‖1≤δ(P)‖z‖1 for every z∈H.
For finite column-stochastic P and m≥1, if q=δ(P^m)<1, P has a unique stationary probability π and every column probability x satisfies ‖x−π‖1≤‖P^mx−x‖1/(1−q)≤m‖Px−x‖1/(1−q).
A finite irreducible row-stochastic K on a nonempty set has a unique positive invariant probability π, and every real row vector w satisfying wK=w is a scalar multiple of π.

Under the stated finite escape hypothesis, N=(I−T)⁻¹=Σ_k≥0 T^k≥0 and ‖N‖∞≤L/ε. First-exit probabilities and mean exit lengths are h=Nb and t=N1, with their errors bounded by L/ε times the respective equation residual norms.

Every invariant probability is a convex mixture of the closed-class invariant probabilities. For initial row law u, the Cesàro averages converge to that mixture with α_j=u(C_j)+u_U(I−T)⁻¹b_j when U is nonempty, and α_j=u(C_j) otherwise.
